difficulty.notes: The 9-xiaomi capture (unlike 8-xiaomi) is NOT string-array obfuscated. The anchor is the account-login params flow (the 1.json answer): a regenerator function in the 2395 login chunk whose case-10 lazy-imports the crypto module (module 23963), encrypts the username via k=m({user:d}) (m=f.encryptAes->Q) and binds w=k.encryptedParams into the request it posts. The AES encryptor Q lives cross-file in a dedicated crypto chunk (crypto.17efe504.chunk.js), exposed as encryptAes()->Q; it is graded as a nested target-specific helper (0.7). encryptAes (accessor) is 0.2; the sibling RSA encryptor B (rsa()->B) builds encryptedParams too but is the RSA path, not the username AES path (off-chain 0). Cross-file oracle: anchor in the 2395 chunk, crypto helpers in the crypto chunk (each role graded in its own file).

task_contract.anchor_definition: The account-login params flow (the 1.json answer, a regenerator function in the 2395 chunk): it lazy-loads the crypto module, encrypts the username via k=m({user:d}) (m=encryptAes->Q) and binds w=k.encryptedParams into the request it posts. Q (the cross-file AES encryptor) 0.7, encryptAes (accessor) 0.2, B (sibling RSA encryptor) 0 are graded below it.

behavior_category.subtype: AES of username into the encryptedParams request field
behavior_category.recompute_check: AES key/iv parsing is internal; not asserted to a fixed value here

near_categories.why_not: A single credential field (username) is tokenized; this is per-field token derivation.
The value is AES of user input, not a device/browser digest.

evidence: The AES encryptor is one of two functions (Q vs B) in a dedicated crypto chunk reached by lazy import; the call site is in another chunk.
Two encryptors Q (AES) and B (RSA) both return encryptedParams; the username uses the AES one.
The encryptor is reached through encryptAes() accessor and a regenerator-compiled async login handler.
